# WasteLens - Project Report

*Auto-generated by `src/evaluate.py` on 2026-09-12 15:00 UTC. Edit freely; sections 3 and 4 are computed from the test set.*

## 1. Introduction

WasteLens is a browser-based waste/garbage image classifier (see PROJECT_BRIEF.md). The user captures or uploads a photo and a client-side TensorFlow.js model classifies it into one of four bins - recyclable, organic, hazardous, or general trash - with a confidence score. This report documents the training data, model, and per-class evaluation results.

## 2. Methodology

- **Dataset:** Kaggle `mostafaabla/garbage-classification` (12 classes), loaded via kagglehub. Remapped to the 4-bin taxonomy; `clothes` and `shoes` dropped. 8,213 usable images.
- **Class mapping:** cardboard/paper/plastic/metal/brown-glass/green-glass/white-glass -> recyclable; biological -> organic; battery -> hazardous; trash -> general trash (docs/dataset_research.md, section 6).
- **Split:** stratified 70/15/15 (seed=42); train 5749 / val 1231 / test 1233 images.
- **Model:** frozen MobileNetV2 (ImageNet) + GAP -> Dropout(0.2) -> Dense(256) -> Dropout(0.2) -> Dense(4, softmax); 328,964 trainable parameters.
- **Training:** Adam(1e-3), sparse categorical cross-entropy, batch 32, 224x224 inputs preprocessed to [-1, 1], 10 epochs, inverse-frequency class weights (recyclable=0.37, organic=2.09, hazardous=2.17, general trash=2.95) to counter the ~8:1 imbalance.
- **Selected checkpoint:** Checkpoint `wastelens_ep09.keras` was selected as the best model by validation loss (lowest val_loss at epoch 9). Epoch 10 showed early signs of overfitting (train_loss 0.0157 vs val_loss 0.0779), so the final epoch was NOT used.

## 4. Weak-Performing Class Analysis

The weakest bin by F1 is **general trash** (F1 = 0.9577; precision = 0.9358, recall = 0.9808).

Where it goes (most frequent confusions):

- true `general trash` predicted as `recyclable`: 1 images (1.0% of its 104 test images)
- true `general trash` predicted as `hazardous`: 1 images (1.0% of its 104 test images)

Plausible explanation (consistent with docs/dataset_research.md, section 5): in the mapped dataset `general trash` has 697 images overall (8.5% of the 8,213 usable images), versus 5,586 for recyclable - an ~8:1 max/min imbalance. Smaller support means the model sees fewer and more varied examples of this bin and, for general trash specifically, it is an open-ended catch-all (miscellaneous items that fit no other bin), so it overlaps visually with every other class. The off-diagonal confusions above show exactly which bins it gets mistaken for; training-time class weights already up-weighted it (weight = 2.95), which mitigates but cannot fully remove the imbalance effect.

## 5. Conclusion

On the held-out test set the frozen-backbone transfer model reached accuracy = 0.9822 and macro-F1 = 0.9742 (weighted-F1 = 0.9822). The per-class results and confusion matrix above satisfy the project success criteria; the flagged weak bin and its analysis (section 4) document the main limitation.
